title: A virtual proxy that loads the image once, on first real use

blocks.text: The page's virtual proxy stands in for an expensive `RealImageService` and creates it only when it is really needed. The client sees the same `ImageService` interface either way. Its pitfalls section adds a warning: a lazy `if (service == null)` check is a race when threads share the proxy.

Given: `ImageService` (`display()`, `getFilename()`, `getSize()`). Write `VirtualImageProxy implements ImageService`. The constructor takes the filename and a `loader` (`Function<String, ImageService>`) that builds the real image, so the tests can count loads.

items: The constructor loads nothing, but **a blank filename is refused in the constructor** with `IllegalArgumentException`.
**`getFilename` does not load the image**: the proxy already knows it.

`display()` and `getSize()` load the image on first use and delegate to it. **The image is loaded once and reused**, and even when **racing first calls** come from two threads, **they load the image once**.
`isLoaded()` says whether the real image exists yet.

cases.says: Creating the proxy loads nothing; display() loads the real image and returns its answer, and isLoaded() then says true.
getFilename() answers from the proxy without loading the image.
display(), getSize() and display() again load the image once and reuse it.
When a second thread calls display() while the first is still loading, the loader still runs once and both get the same answer.
new VirtualImageProxy("  ", loader) throws IllegalArgumentException in the constructor, before any load.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A proxy implements the same interface as the real subject, so the client cannot tell the two apart.
A virtual proxy shared between threads must make its lazy creation thread-safe, for example with double-checked locking on a volatile field.
A virtual proxy creates the expensive real subject only on first real use, answers what it already knows itself, and reuses the subject afterwards.
